stem: How many 3-letter codes can be formed from the letters of the word MOTHER, with no letter used more than once in any code?

per_option_rationale.rationale: MOTHER has 6 distinct letters. Ordered selection of 3 from 6 without repetition = P(6, 3) = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120.
Computed C(6, 3) = 20 as if the code order does not matter, treating the selection as unordered.
Computed 6! = 720, using all 6 letters of MOTHER in every code instead of selecting 3 from 6.
Computed 6^3 = 216, allowing repetition as if letters could be reused, instead of using P(6,3) without repetition.

explanation: MOTHER: 6 distinct letters. A 3-letter code cares about order (MO is different from OM) and uses no letter twice. This is P(6, 3) = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120.

explanation_sections.punchline: A code is ordered and no repetition is allowed: P(6,3) = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: order matters (codes AM and MA are different) + no repetition -> permutation formula. P(n, r) = n x (n-1) x (n-2) for r = 3. Here 6 x 5 x 4 = 120.
explanation_sections.lesson: The decision tree: does order matter? If yes, use permutation P(n,r). Can you reuse? If no, it is P without repetition. If yes, it is n^r.
explanation_sections.timing: 50-60 s. The two traps are C(6,3) = 20 (order forgotten) and 6^3 = 216 (repetition allowed). The word 'code' implies order matters since codes are sequences.
